after_hours_whatsapp.description: A Gallabox WhatsApp to this person's phone the moment a fresh lead lands on them, any time of day, so they can call then and there. Set for Harrsha, 1 Oct 2026 (first 7 PM to 10 AM only, widened to all hours the same day). Field name kept for compatibility.
after_hours_whatsapp.title: WhatsApp on every fresh lead

also_site_executive.description: Anugna and Charan work the phone and the site. One login, two halves, scored separately.
also_site_executive.title: Also handles site visits

attendance_exempt.description: Founders and anyone else who does not punch. Their days are never computed or deducted.
attendance_exempt.title: Not tracked for attendance

can_edit_projects.description: Lets a person who is not admin, marketing or a project owner edit project details and pricing. Set for Sukanya on 15 Sep 2026.
can_edit_projects.title: Can edit project pricing and sales kit

email.title: Work email, used for the invite

escalation_head_for.description: Terrace 35 has four project heads and only Gowtham takes the late leads, so whichever head the database happens to return first is not an answer.
escalation_head_for.title: Projects where late leads come to this person

full_name.title: Full name as it should appear in the app

full_time_wfh.description: Punches from anywhere are accepted with GPS and selfie, flagged wfh, with no office fence and no HR site check. Hours, late logins and LOP follow the normal office rules. Does not use up the monthly WFH allowance. Set for Lavanya on 26 Sep 2026.
full_time_wfh.title: Works from home full time

head_for_project_codes.description: A BDR who also runs a project gets the head's visibility for these projects without changing their primary role. They stay on the rota as a BDR and see the head's view here. Edited by an admin in the app.
head_for_project_codes.title: Projects this person runs as head

head_for_project_ids.description: Pushed onto the linked User record so the role-independent RLS branch on Lead, Visit, Task, Spend and AuditLog matches without a role check.
head_for_project_ids.title: Head-for project ids, resolved from the codes

invited_by.description: The login email of the admin who added them on the Team page. Added 3 Oct 2026.
invited_by.title: Admin who added this person

joined_on.description: The day this person starts. Attendance is not computed for any day before it, and the Booking Scorecard clock cannot start before it. Empty for everyone who was on the team before 3 Oct 2026, which changes nothing for them.
joined_on.title: Joining date, IST

legacy_names.description: Azeez is four people in the source, Venkat is three. This is how they become one.
legacy_names.title: Every spelling used in the sheets

meeting_project_codes.description: Who a BDR can pick under 'Who ran it' when logging Meeting held on this project. Separate from visits because heads run the closing meetings and site executives walk the site. Unset falls back to the old role rule. Added 19 Sep 2026.
meeting_project_codes.title: Projects where this person runs meetings

project_codes.description: What this person can see. Must include every project they have history on, which is why it is wider than rota_projects. Edited by an admin in the app, not derived from code.
project_codes.title: Projects this person works

project_ids.description: Pushed onto the linked User record so RLS sees the change the moment the admin saves, without waiting for a reseed.
project_ids.title: Project ids, resolved from the codes

reporting_manager_member_id.description: Who approves this person's leave, WFH, comp off and punch corrections in Attendance. Admin and founder can approve for anyone. Added 24 Sep 2026.
reporting_manager_member_id.title: Reporting manager, a TeamMember id

role.description: The working role. A BDR stays a BDR here even when they also run a project as its head, so they keep taking new leads on the rota. The head grant is separate, in head_for_project_codes.
role.title: Primary role

rota_projects.description: Deliberately not the same as project_codes. project_codes is what somebody can see, which must include every project they have history on. This is what lands on them tomorrow morning, which is the founder's decision and must never be inferred. Empty means no new leads. Edited by an admin in the app; a reseed no longer overwrites it.
rota_projects.title: Projects this person takes NEW leads for

rota_weight.description: New joiners run at 0.5 until told otherwise.
rota_weight.title: Share of round robin assignment

screens_project_codes.description: After a call on one of these projects they get a Hand to step, and any lead they hand on stays in their Leads with them under Handled by. Routing itself is the rota: they sit alone on the project's rota. Set for Harrsha on Oxygen Forest, 1 Oct 2026.
screens_project_codes.title: Projects where this person speaks to every fresh lead first

status.description: mapped means the book is ready and waiting, nobody has been invited yet.
status.title: Where this person is in the rollout

takes_leads.description: False means nothing in the routing engine may put a lead on this person: not the rota, not an escalation rung, not the founder fallback at the floor of the ladder. Leadership and marketing are set false. Different from active, which is whether they are still with the firm, and from rota_projects, which is what lands on them tomorrow. Added 9 Sep 2026 after the ladder's floor fell through to the first admin by name.
takes_leads.title: Can be handed a lead

user_id.title: Linked login, set by an admin at approval

visit_project_codes.description: Who a BDR can pick under 'Who is taking them' when logging Visit booked or Visit done on this project. Must be a subset of project_codes. Unset (never saved) falls back to the old role rule. Added 19 Sep 2026.
visit_project_codes.title: Projects where this person takes site visits

wrap_reports.description: The team level marketing wrap up and sales wrap up on WhatsApp at 8 PM, on top of any personal message. Set for Arjun, Swathi and Harrsha, 1 Oct 2026.
wrap_reports.title: Gets the 8 PM marketing and sales reports

cancel_reason.title: Why the visit was cancelled, e.g. buyer said no (28 Oct 2026)

owner_member_id.title: BDR who owns the lead, a TeamMember id

time_set.description: 6 Oct 2026. A visit booked with no time is stored at 10:00 IST as a placeholder. True only when somebody picked the time, which is what lets the desk tell the buyer the time on WhatsApp.
time_set.title: A real time was picked for this visit

visited_on.title: Day the buyer came to site, IST YYYY-MM-DD (28 Oct 2026). Growth counts a visit on this day; completed_date is when it was marked.

wa_confirmed_for.description: 6 Oct 2026. The scheduled_date the hoi_visit_confirmed template was sent for. A visit moved to a new time is confirmed again, once.
wa_confirmed_for.title: Visit confirmation sent to the buyer for this scheduled time

wa_reminded_for.description: 6 Oct 2026. The IST day the hoi_visit_reminder template was sent for.
wa_reminded_for.title: Visit reminder sent to the buyer for this IST day

gallabox_template.title: Approved Gallabox template name, for automatic sends later

project_code.title: Only for this project code, blank for all

why.title: What this message is trying to do, shown to the rep

entity_schema.description: This week on the floor, anonymised. One row per IST week, built by the fieldNotes function when anyone signed in presses Build (one model call, at most once a week; never automatic). Holds only patterns: situations backed by at least three different buyers, and the questions buyers kept asking. Never raw notes, names, phones, units or lead ids: every person is removed in code before the model reads anything, and the output is checked again for names, contact details and copied sentences. Feeds Arjun's people-skills drafts, the morning brief's buyer questions, and overheard-line hooks.
entity_schema.name: FieldNote

buyers_read.title: Different buyers in the notes read

notes.title: What was left out and why

count.title: Different buyers behind it, at least 3

entity_schema.description: Read-only context imported from the team's Google Sheets on 26 Aug 2026. One row per sheet row, NOT one per lead: a lead often appears in several tabs and each appearance says something different. Nothing here drives routing, counting, the rota, the two hour clock or escalation. It exists so a BDR opening a lead can see what already happened to that person instead of searching six workbooks. Raw values are always kept beside any cleaned value, because the source columns mix dates, statuses and free text in the same cell.
entity_schema.name: LeadHistory

campaign_raw.description: Source sheet, campaign id, ad payload or page URL, whatever that tab carried.
campaign_raw.title: Where it came from

handled_by.description: The sheets carry about 25 spellings for 15 people. This is the canonical name.
handled_by.title: Who worked it, cleaned

handled_by_raw.title: Who worked it, exactly as written

last_contacted_raw.description: Day level, usually with no year, in at least seven formats. Some cells contain a status instead of a date. Never parsed into a real date field, because guessing here is how history becomes fiction.
last_contacted_raw.title: Last contacted, verbatim

lead_id.description: The Lead this row was matched to, by the last ten digits of the phone. Empty when the number matched no lead, matched more than one, or was unusable. Those rows are still stored so a BDR can search a number that is not in the book.
lead_id.title: Lead id

person_name.title: Name as written in the sheet

phone_raw.description: Kept because some cells hold #ERROR!, an email address, or a nine digit number.
phone_raw.title: Phone exactly as the sheet had it

remarks.description: Every remark column on the row, labelled and joined. This is the part a BDR actually needs.
remarks.title: Remarks and notes

sheet_row.description: So the original row can be found again.
sheet_row.title: Row number in that tab

status_raw.description: Deliberately not normalised. The six workbooks use roughly 60 strings for about 12 real states and collapsing them would lose meaning.
status_raw.title: Status, verbatim

lead_assigned_to_id.description: The login of the lead's owner, copied here because it decides who can read the row. 5 Oct 2026, bug audit (L2): the server now moves it when the lead changes hands (shared/handover.ts, mergeLeads), and the login it names can read the row whatever their role. Before this only a BDR could, so a site executive or project head who was handed a lead from another project saw none of its history.
lead_assigned_to_id.title: BDR assigned to the lead (denormalised)

outcome.title: Outcome (connected, no_answer, callback, not_interested, qualified, booked)

performed_by_id.title: User id who performed the activity

performed_by_member_id.title: Who did it, a TeamMember id

ad_campaign_name.title: Campaign name at the time the lead arrived

ai_call_attempt_id.title: Sarvam attempt id of the latest call

ai_call_interaction_id.title: Sarvam interaction id, for the recording

ai_call_language.title: Language the buyer spoke on the AI call

ai_call_next_at.title: When the queued AI call is due

ai_call_note.title: Why the AI call was skipped, queued or failed

ai_call_outcome.title: AI call outcome (qualified, callback_requested, not_interested, no_answer...)

ai_call_state.description: Where Sarvam's qualifying call stands. Empty means AI calling never applied to this lead.
ai_call_state.title: Priya's AI call

ai_call_summary.title: What the buyer told Priya, in brief

ai_do_not_call.title: Buyer asked not to get automated calls

also_pitching.description: 19 Sep 2026. The lead stays on its main project (project_id) with one owner; these are the other projects the same buyer is considering. Added by the owner in the lead panel, or automatically when the buyer enquires through another project's ad or form. Never moves spend, never changes the owner.
also_pitching.title: Other projects this buyer is being shown

alt_phone.description: 19 Sep 2026. The main phone is the permanent key and never edited; a second number the buyer gives goes here. Set only through editLead.
alt_phone.title: Alternate phone, added by the team

booking_confirmed_at.title: When the project head confirmed it

booking_ref.description: Unit 1903, 2057 sqyds, whatever identifies the thing sold. Typed when Sale closed is tapped. Until now this only ever existed as free text in a remark, which is why nobody could list what had actually been sold.
booking_ref.title: What they bought

booking_state.description: 21 Sep 2026. Written only by bookingDesk. awaiting = booked, waiting for the project head to confirm payment. confirmed = project head confirmed payment. cancelled = booking cancelled. Status stays booked for awaiting and confirmed, so every existing screen still sees it.
booking_state.title: Where the booking stands

booking_units.description: 21 Sep 2026. One buyer can book two units; each unit is its own Booking and counts once. Kept by bookingDesk.
booking_units.title: Confirmed units booked on this lead

booking_units_awaiting.title: Units booked but not confirmed yet

booking_units_cp.title: Confirmed units closed through a CP

booking_via_cp.title: A live booking on this lead was closed through a channel partner

call_attempts.description: Incremented by the No answer outcome. A missed call is not progress, so it must not move the status: a lead that has been rung four times with no answer is still assigned, and saying so on the row is more useful than inventing a status for it.
call_attempts.title: Times somebody tried and got no answer

client_id.description: 6 Oct 2026. One permanent, internal ID per buyer, so two people with the same name can be told apart without comparing phone numbers. A plain running number with no project or year in it, because a lead moves between projects. Written only by the server (base44/shared/clientId.ts): at creation for every door, and by the sweep for anything that missed. Never changes on an edit, a transfer or a project move, and is never shown to the buyer. A merged copy keeps the ID it had; the lead it was merged into keeps its own.
client_id.title: Client ID, e.g. HOI-004217

client_id_at.title: When the Client ID was issued

details_edited_at.title: When name, email or alternate number was last edited

details_edited_by.title: Who last edited name, email or alternate number

enquiry_date.title: Original enquiry date from the sheets

escalated.title: Has been escalated at least once

escalated_from_member_id.title: Who held it before the escalation

escalation_chain.title: Every member who has held this lead

escalation_level.title: Which rung of the ladder it is on

first_enquiry_date.title: The first enquiry date, kept when a repeat enquiry moves enquiry_date forward

fit_at.title: When the Better fit was last worked out

fit_from.title: What raised it: rating or not_buying

fit_note.title: Why the buyer does not fit their own project, in a few words

fit_project_ids.description: 16 Oct 2026, cross-sell. Written only by the server (functions/crossSell, rules in shared/crossSell.ts) when the buyer rating is saved or the lead is marked Not buying for price, location or timing. At most two, best first. Saved once, so no list or screen works it out again.
fit_project_ids.title: Better fit: projects that suit this buyer better than their own

fit_state.description: suggested = shown on the lead, waiting for the owner. added = the project went under Also showing and a Pitch task was written. dismissed = the owner tapped Not now; the same projects are not suggested again.
fit_state.title: Better fit: where it stands

handlers.description: 5 Oct 2026, bug audit (L5): credit is written only by the server (creditHandler, transferOwner, mergeLeads), so a browser update of this list is refused. It also decides who can read the lead.
handlers.title: Everybody who has handled this lead

heat_manual.description: Optional. The automatic heat is the default. A rep can override it; the override lapses after 14 days or when the status changes, and the automatic score takes over again.
heat_manual.title: Heat set by hand

heat_manual_at.title: When the heat was set by hand

heat_manual_by.title: Who set the heat by hand

heat_manual_status.title: Lead status when the heat was set by hand

is_nri.description: Set when the lead arrived with a foreign E.164 phone number (+971, +966, +1, +44, etc.). These are genuine NRI enquiries, not data errors. Since 15 Sep 2026 they follow the project rota like any other lead.
is_nri.title: Non-resident Indian, foreign phone number

is_organic.title: Came from an unpaid form, not an ad

last_inbound_lead_id.title: Platform lead id of the latest repeat submission, so a reconcile never restarts the clock twice

last_note.title: Latest note a person wrote (copied from Activity, see shared/lastNote.ts)

last_note_at.title: When the latest note was written

last_note_type.title: Activity type of the latest note

legacy_owner.title: Owner name from the sheets, resolved to a user id once logins exist

legacy_source_sheet.title: Which sheet or register this came from

lost_reason.description: Set when Sale lost is tapped. Status still goes to dropped, because dropped is what every screen counts, but dropped currently holds a quarter of the whole book and lumps junk callers in with buyers lost to a competitor after a site visit. This is what separates them without touching the status enum.
lost_reason.title: Why the sale was lost

merged_into_lead_id.title: This lead was a duplicate and was merged into this one

name_original.description: Stamped the first time the name is edited, never rewritten, so a corrected Meta lead can still be matched in Ads Manager.
name_original.title: Name as the lead arrived

nc_attempts.description: Added 5 Oct 2026. Counts No answer and Busy since nc_since. Goes back to 0 when the run ends. call_attempts is the count for the whole life of the lead and is never reset.
nc_attempts.title: Unanswered attempts in the current run

nc_since.description: Added 5 Oct 2026 for the telecaller cadence. Set on the first No answer or Busy of a run and left alone until the buyer is reached or the lead is closed, when it is cleared. The next try is worked out from how many days have passed since this day: week 1 twice a day, week 2 alternate days, weeks 3 and 4 once a week, then the lead closes as not reachable. Blank means no run is open.
nc_since.title: First unanswered attempt of the current run, IST day YYYY-MM-DD

owner_called_at.description: 24 Oct 2026. A lead handed to a new owner kept its old stage (qualified, visited), so the home screen treated it as already called when the new owner had never rung it. Stamped by the browser when the owner logs a call, and by the server sweep (shared/callStamp.ts) from the Activity log. A lead counts as not called yet for its owner while this is older than assigned_date.
owner_called_at.title: Last time the current owner called or met this buyer

project_history.title: Project codes this lead has been pitched

project_id.description: 5 Oct 2026, bug audit (L5): no screen changes this on an existing lead. It moves only through the server (Move to another project, Transfer, make main project, merge), so a browser update of it is refused. Setting it when a lead is created is not affected.
project_id.title: Project of interest

reenquiry_date.title: When this person last came back through an ad or form. Restarts the two hour clock

referral_note.title: How the referrer knows the buyer

registration_type.description: 21 Sep 2026. Set by Add lead. Before this field existed every hand registered lead was saved as a walk in and the referral details were dropped.
registration_type.title: How a hand registered lead came in

score_answered.title: Lead score: how many of the eight questions are answered

score_at.title: Lead score: when it was last saved

score_by.title: Lead score: who last saved it

score_category.description: Written with the answers, for lists and reports. Blank until all eight are answered, unless a disqualifier is set or the buyer said after 6 months. The screens work it out again from the answers, so this copy never decides what a person sees.
score_category.title: Lead score: category (hot, warm, cold, later, unqualified)

score_decision.title: Lead score: decision maker (sole, main, shared, none)

score_disqualifier.description: One of the six automatic disqualifiers on the founder's sheet: budget, location, authority, price_only, not_interested, other_need. Any one makes the lead Unqualified. Blank means none.
score_disqualifier.title: Lead score: why this is not a buyer for us

score_handover.title: Lead score: handover, or registration for land (m3, m3_6, m6, none)

score_location.title: Lead score: location (match, nearby, vague, other)

score_payment.title: Lead score: payment (ready, plan, open, none)

score_period.title: Lead score: when they will buy (d30, m1_3, m3_6, m6, undecided)

score_size.title: Lead score: size, or plot size for land (match, flex, vague, nomatch)

score_ticket.description: 7 Oct 2026. The founder's lead score, eight answers a caller taps on the lead (src/lib/leadScore.js). Each answer is saved as its short code, not as points, so the wording or the points can change later without touching a lead. Blank means not answered.
score_ticket.title: Lead score: budget (match, near, far, none)

score_total.title: Lead score: points so far, out of 24

score_visit.title: Lead score: site visit (d7, d30, later, no)

screened_by_member_id.description: Set by transferOwner when the person handing the lead on screens that project (TeamMember.screens_project_codes). Keeps the lead in their Leads under Mine after it leaves their book. Added 1 Oct 2026 for Harrsha on Oxygen Forest. 5 Oct 2026, bug audit (L17): this person can now read the lead through this field alone, so being taken off Handled by no longer hides it from them. Written only by the server.
screened_by_member_id.title: Spoke first and handed it on, a TeamMember id

site_visit_date.title: Site visit date from the sheets

source_project_code.title: Project that originally paid for this lead

wa_ack_at.description: 6 Oct 2026. Stamped by the server (base44/shared/buyerWa.ts) when the hoi_enquiry_received template goes to the buyer. One per lead, ever.
wa_ack_at.title: Enquiry acknowledgement sent to the buyer on WhatsApp at

wa_missed_since.description: 6 Oct 2026. Holds the nc_since of the run the hoi_missed_call template was sent for, so each run of unanswered calls sends it once.
wa_missed_since.title: Missed call WhatsApp sent for the run that began on this IST day

wa_opt_out.description: 6 Oct 2026. Set by the server when the buyer replies STOP (or the like) on WhatsApp. While true the desk sends this buyer no WhatsApp by itself (base44/shared/buyerWa.ts). A rep can still message from their own phone.
wa_opt_out.title: The buyer asked not to be messaged on WhatsApp

wa_opt_out_at.title: When the buyer asked not to be messaged

assigned_by_member_id.title: Who assigned it, a TeamMember id

assigned_by_name.title: Who assigned it, name at the time

auto_ref.description: Added 7 Oct 2026. Set only on the follow ups the desk writes by itself (src/lib/autoFollowUps.js): visit:<visit id>:reconfirm:<day>, visit:<visit id>:feedback, booking:<booking id>:docs. One task per value, so the same follow up is never written twice.
auto_ref.title: Automatic follow up, what it is for

collaborator_member_ids.description: People working on the task alongside the assignee. They see it in My tasks and can update or close it. Added 29 Sep 2026.
collaborator_member_ids.title: Collaborators, TeamMember ids

collaborator_user_ids.description: Resolved from collaborator_member_ids so row level security matches the login.
collaborator_user_ids.title: Collaborators, login ids

due_time.description: Added 5 Oct 2026. The time of day the follow up is due, in IST, 24 hour, for example 16:30. Blank means any time that day.
due_time.title: Due time, IST HH:MM, optional

reason.description: Added 5 Oct 2026. A short code, not a sentence: no_answer for an automatic try again, or one of the call back reasons in src/lib/cadence.js such as busy_now, call_later, family, budget or loan.
reason.title: Why this follow up, a short code

entity_schema.description: One row every time a scheduled job runs. Exists because five jobs were configured, published and believed in for four days while none of them ever fired, and nothing anywhere said so. A job that reports nothing is indistinguishable from a job that has nothing to report.
entity_schema.name: JobRun

caller.description: Kept so the platform's own scheduler can be recognised the first time it fires, rather than guessed at.
caller.title: The headers this run arrived with

job.description: The function name for a run. Since 5 Oct 2026 a name with a colon is a note a job keeps so it never does the same thing twice, not a run: dailyWrap:day (today's wrap was started), dailyWrap:sent (one row per WhatsApp that went), sarvamWebhook:claim (one row per AI call result taken in), pushGoogleConversions:pushed (one row per visit Google accepted). Do not delete these.
job.title: Function name

summary.description: Since 5 Oct 2026 a run first writes 'started <run id>' and rewrites the same row with what it did when it ends. A 'started' row that never changes is a run that was cut off. Where the row could not be rewritten, a second row 'finished <run id> ...' closes it. This is how a second copy of a job knows to step aside (shared/heartbeat.ts).
summary.title: What it did, in one line

trigger.description: The whole point. A run started by a person proves the code works. Only a run started by the schedule proves the schedule works. The default was 'schedule' until 25 Aug 2026, when it turned out every curl fired during a check was being recorded as the clock and systemHealth was reporting a job as healthy that had never once run on its own. Nothing counts as scheduled now without a header that says so.
trigger.title: What started it

entity_schema.description: The finished PNG of a news card, kept in rows of base64 so the newsCard function can serve it at a public link for WhatsApp. Separate from NewsCard so listing cards never drags the picture along.
entity_schema.name: NewsCardPhoto

entity_schema.description: 28 Oct 2026. One row: HOI's Google review link that the ask message carries. Set by an admin on the Google reviews screen, written only by the server.
entity_schema.name: ReviewSetting

review_link.title: House of Investors Google review link

approval_status.description: A new signup lands pending and can read nothing until an admin approves it.
approval_status.title: Admin approval

head_for_project_ids.description: Pushed from the TeamMember card by teamAdmin and the login sync. The access rules on Lead, Visit, Task, Booking and AuditLog read it. Written by the code since Sep 2026 and added to this schema on 5 Oct 2026.
head_for_project_ids.title: Project ids this user runs as head

member_id.description: Set by an admin at approval. Until it is set the login sees nothing.
member_id.title: Which TeamMember this login is

project_ids.title: Project ids this user belongs to
